headline: Project Mind turns your GitHub history into searchable AI memory
summary: This AI-powered system uses local inference to create a knowledge base from your code, documentation, and discussions, keeping sensitive data private.
details: Project Mind is an AI-powered memory and question-answering system designed for GitHub repositories. It transforms scattered project knowledge—decisions, bugs, fixes, discussions, and context—into a searchable database.

Developers can ask natural language questions about their projects, such as how authentication flows or the history of specific bugs. Project Mind retrieves relevant parts of the actual project and explains the flow with source references.

The system collects source files, documentation, issues, pull requests, commits, and approved memories from a connected repository. Users can see which sources have been indexed and where the information originated.

Crucially, Project Mind uses open-weight AI and local inference via Ollama and Llama 3.2 3B. This ensures that sensitive project data, like private source code or internal documentation, is not sent to external AI services.

Embeddings are generated locally using Nomic Embed Text, and the data is stored in MongoDB Atlas. The retrieved context is then processed by the local Llama model to generate answers, with sources clearly displayed.

The project emphasizes that important knowledge isn't always in the code itself. Explicitly saved memories, like security decisions regarding token handling, can be retrieved alongside implementation details.

By utilizing local inference, Project Mind offers developers greater control over AI processing and the system's architecture. This approach enables the creation of project-specific memory systems built around open models and tools.

headline_marked: Tesla adds [[Emergency Drive Away]] feature for Supercharger incidents
headline: Tesla adds Emergency Drive Away feature for Supercharger incidents
summary: New software update allows drivers to disengage from Superchargers in urgent situations, following a recent shooting incident.
details: Tesla has rolled out an "Emergency Drive Away" feature, enabling drivers to shift into Drive even while still connected to a Supercharger. This update comes in response to a shooting incident where a driver was unable to quickly exit their vehicle.

To activate the feature, drivers must unlock the charge port via the infotainment system, app, or a button on the charger handle. If attempting to drive away while plugged in, the infotainment system will display a warning about potential damage to the car and the Supercharger station.
The feature requires updating to the latest Tesla software and is currently exclusive to Superchargers in the US. Older models, specifically pre-2021 Model S and X vehicles, are not supported.

Tesla warns that deliberate misuse of the Emergency Drive Away feature will result in penalties, with potential electrical and civil costs reaching up to $25,000. It remains unclear if Tesla will charge for activating the feature in genuine emergencies.
